title: openetl declarative source manifest
description: A source for an HTTP API, as data. Expressions are CEL. Templates are text with {expression} holes; {{ and }} are literal braces. A template that is one hole keeps the hole's value: null leaves a parameter or header out, and a list repeats a parameter.

metadata.description: Which connector and version this is, and what the console shows about it.

name.description: The connector's package: owner/name, or name for the official owner, openetl. Each part is lowercase letters, digits and hyphens.

license.description: An SPDX expression, such as Apache-2.0.

repository.description: An https URL of the source repository.

tags.description: Words the catalog shows with the connector, such as crm.

logo.description: An https URL of the connector's logo, which the UI shows.

release.description: The git release this version comes from.

url.description: An https URL, such as the release's page.

spec.description: The source: its config, how it calls the API, and its streams.

resources.description: What the source asks of its jobs.

hint.description: The job size a pipeline of this source starts at when it's sized automatically.

config.description: The JSON Schema of the connector's config: an object. Top-level string properties with x-secret: true are secrets, which only auth and sign can reference, by name. Expressions see the other properties as config.NAME.

properties.description: The config's properties, by name, each a JSON Schema.

check.description: What Check does: fetch the first page of a stream. Default: the first stream without a parent.

stream.description: The stream whose first page Check fetches.

templates.description: Names, each with a template, such as a request's query parameters.

secret.description: A config property marked x-secret, by name.
The name of a config property marked x-secret.

http.description: How the source calls the API: its base URL, headers, auth, signing, rate limit and error rules.

base_url.description: A template over config. Request paths are appended to it, and next-page URLs must have its scheme, host and port.

headers.description: Headers for every request: templates, as in a stream's request.

rate_limit.description: How fast the source sends requests.

rps.description: Requests per second at most. The rate adapts below it when the API throttles.

errors.description: Error rules for every stream, after the stream's own.

auth.description: How requests authenticate. The host adds the credential when a request leaves, and only to the base URL's scheme, host and port.

header.description: The header the key goes in, such as X-API-Key.

query.description: The query parameter the key goes in.

prefix.description: Put before the key, such as "Token ".

refresh_token.description: A refresh token, for the refresh token grant. Without one, the host uses the client credentials grant.

auth_style.description: Where the client credentials go in token requests. Default: the host tries both.

session_token.description: An AWS session token, for temporary credentials.

service.description: The AWS service's signing name, such as execute-api.

sign.description: Signs every request with a key the host holds. hmac puts a MAC of message in a header or a query parameter; jwt sends a JWT as the Authorization header.

message.description: An expression over request (method, url, path, query, headers, body), config and now, returning a string or bytes.

header.description: The header the MAC goes in.

query.description: The query parameter the MAC goes in.

claims.description: An expression over config and now, returning a map.

jose_header.description: An expression returning extra header fields, such as kid. The host sets alg and typ.

stream.description: A stream the source reads: how to request it, page through it, and find its records.

primary_key.description: The top-level properties that make up a record's primary key.

records.description: An expression over response, returning the page's records, each an object. Default: response.body.

parent.description: Read the stream once per record of another stream, which the request sees as parent. The parent must have a primary key and no parent of its own.

partitions.description: Read the stream in splits, concurrently where the job has room, each with its own place and floor. Requests see each one as partition. Not for a stream with a parent.

values.description: An expression over config and now, returning a list: a partition per entry.

range.description: Partitions of {start, end}, in RFC 3339, a step at a time.

start.description: An expression over config and now, returning a timestamp.

errors.description: Error rules for this stream, tried before the API's.

schema.description: JSON Schema for some or all of the record's top-level properties, which declares their types. The others are inferred.

properties.description: The properties' JSON Schemas, by name.

request.description: Templates over config, state, page, parent, partition and now.

path.description: Appended to the base URL. Holes are escaped as path segments.

body.description: An expression whose value is sent as JSON.

idempotent.description: Lets the host retry a POST, such as a search that changes nothing.

paginator.description: How to get the next page. A resume point follows every page. Without a paginator, a stream is one page.

type.description: How the next page is found.

stop.description: An expression over response and records; true ends pagination.

next.description: An expression over response and records: the next page's token, or null or an empty string at the end. Requests see it as page.token.

param.description: Also send the token as this query parameter.

next.description: An expression over response and records: the next page's URL, absolute or relative to the base URL, or null or an empty string at the end. It's fetched as it is, with no params added.

then.description: The next page is the Link header's rel="next" URL, fetched as it is.

size.description: Records in a full page. A shorter page is the last.

size_param.description: Send size as this query parameter.

size.description: Records in a full page. A shorter page is the last.

size_param.description: Send size as this query parameter.

incremental.description: Read from a cursor floor onwards. Requests see the floor, less the lookback, as state.cursor, which is absent on the first sync. The API must return every record whose cursor is at or after it.

cursor_field.description: A top-level property of the records.

type.description: `datetime`: RFC 3339 text, and `state.cursor` is a timestamp. `unix`: seconds since 1970, and `state.cursor` is an int. `integer` and `string`: compared as they are.

lookback.description: Read again this far behind the floor, for late updates. datetime and unix only.

ordered.description: The API returns records sorted by the cursor, oldest first, so the floor advances after every page.

errors.description: Rules tried in order on every response. The first whose when is true decides; an expression that fails to evaluate doesn't match.

action.description: `fail`: fail with `code` and `message`. `ignore`: treat the response as an empty last page. `expired`: the page token a resumed read started from was rejected, so the stream starts over from its floor.

code.description: For fail. Default: how the host classified the response.

message.description: For fail: a template over response.
